rows.jyutping: haang4 dak1 jiu4 jiu4 fong2 fong2
rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for walking or moving unsteadily and nearly falling.

example.english: They were drunk and began to totter along, nearly falling into the road.
example.traditional: 佢飲醉咗，行得搖搖晃晃，差啲跌落馬路。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jam2 zeoi3 zo2 haang4 dak1 jiu4 jiu4 fong2 fong2 caa1 di1 dit3 lok6 maa5 lou6

rows.note: Use this when someone cannot stand steadily, rather than when the main focus is their walking.

example.english: After kneeling all night, my legs were numb and I began to totter as I stood up.
example.traditional: 我跪咗成晚，兩隻腳麻晒，企都企唔穩。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gwai6 zo2 sing4 maan5 loeng5 zek3 goek3 maa4 saai3 kei5 dou1 kei5 m4 wan2

rows.meaning: be on the brink of collapse
rows.note: This is the everyday spoken choice for a person, business, or structure that is about to collapse.

example.english: The company is losing so much money that it may totter on the brink of collapse.
example.jyutping: gaan1 gung1 si1 sit6 dou3 zau6 lai4 lam1
